title: Law requiring big businesses to offer human customer service
summary: This bill would require large private businesses with over $500 million in national annual revenue to let New York City customers easily reach a human customer service agent, generally within 15 minutes or via an appointment within one business day. It would also cap hold times at 15 minutes per instance and one hour cumulatively, and require clear disclosure when customers are interacting with a chatbot rather than a person. Violations would carry civil penalties of $5,000 for a first offense and $10,000 for each subsequent one, and the law would take effect 180 days after enactment.
